text:
Muscle lactate production rises when glycolysis speeds up at the start of exercise, because pyruvate and NADH form faster than mitochondria can oxidize them and more pyruvate is reduced to lactate. Ready oxygen favors oxidation of pyruvate, lactate cannot be made if pyruvate is not formed, and a falling muscle pH slows glycolysis rather than driving it. The answer is D.

CONFIDENCE: 90
